question.prompt: A box contains \(28\) red balls, \(20\) green balls, \(19\) yellow balls, \(13\) blue balls, \(11\) white balls, and \(9\) black balls. What is the minimum number of balls that must be drawn from the box without replacement to guarantee that at least \(15\) balls of a single color will be drawn?

solutions.title: Maximize a draw below the target
solutions.explanation:
Find the largest draw that can still avoid having \(15\) balls of one color.

Such a draw can contain at most \(14\) each of red, green, and yellow. It can also contain all \(13\) blue, \(11\) white, and \(9\) black balls, since none of those colors has \(15\) available. Therefore any draw avoiding the target has at most
\[
14+14+14+13+11+9=75
\]
balls.

This draw is possible with the given supplies, so \(75\) balls do not guarantee the target. Drawing \(76\) balls exceeds that maximum and must give at least \(15\) of some color.

The minimum is \(\boxed{76}\), choice \(\textbf{(B)}\).
